title: KV prewarm & shape-aware footprint synthesis for long-context variants
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: For Llama/Mistral/Qwen variants running at long-context settings we observe a trade-off between aggressive KV prewarm (low cold-start latency) and increased GPU memory pressure that leads to higher OOM risk under continuous batching. This ticket scopes an engineering solution to synthesize model-specific, shape-aware 'prewarm footprints' and a runtime policy that dynamically budgets prewarm memory based on per-variant occupancy models and current batch shape distribution.

Goals:
- Produce per-variant prewarm budgets and slab sizes that minimize cold-start tail latency without exceeding a configurable headroom threshold on target GPU types.
- Integrate a lightweight estimator into the serving runtime that uses recent batch-shape histograms + model profile to predict safe prewarm allocation.
- Ensure compatibility with continuous batching: prewarm should not increase average latency for in-flight requests in high throughput conditions.

Scope:
- Instrument existing batch-shape telemetry and extend the model profiler to capture layer-wise KV residency for representative sequences (short, medium, long).
- Implement a 'prewarm allocator' that can carve ephemeral slabs for KV warmup and release/evict deterministically when memory pressure rises.
- Run targeted experiments across Llama-2-70B longctx, Mistral-8x-16k, Qwen-14-64k variants.

Out of scope:
- Full allocator rewrite; use existing slab allocator API and extend with prewarm reservations.

Success metrics:
- Cold-start p95 token-latency reduced >= 30% for warmup-sensitive routes compared to baseline.
- OOM incidents reduced to zero for controlled replay workloads with prewarm enabled and headroom >= 1.5GB.
- Average tokens/sec degradation under high throughput <= 5% compared to baseline (no prewarm).
acceptance_criteria: Per-variant prewarm profiles generated for Llama-2-70B, Mistral-8x-16k, Qwen-14-64k and uploaded to the model catalog.
Runtime estimator enabled behind feature-flag that respects per-host headroom config and disables prewarm when unsafe.
Experiment results demonstrating required latency and OOM improvements with clear dashboards linked.
Integration tests to simulate continuous batching shapes with/without prewarm and validate no regression >5% TPS.
PRs merged for runtime, profiler extension, and telemetry dashboards; rollout plan documented.
design_notes: Key idea: model-specific 'prewarm shapes' are a small set of representative KV slice patterns (e.g., full-depth long sequence, sparse prefix-heavy, windowed attention) plus an occupancy curve estimating extra slabs needed to reach target warm coverage.
Estimator inputs: recent 10k request shape histogram, model footprint profile (layer-by-layer KV slice sizes), GPU headroom (free bytes) and current slab fragmentation metric.

Allocation policy: greedy prewarm up to min(per-variant-budget, fraction_of_headroom) with LRU-style eviction for ephemeral slabs. If headroom < threshold, prewarm disabled and a telemetry marker emitted.
Co-existence with batching: prewarm logic runs at worker-sync boundaries and only prewarms during low-latency windows or when batching backlog is small (backlog length heuristic).
Fail-safe: when OOM triggers are observed, runtime will automatically disable prewarm and emit a high-severity alert for rollback.
decisions: Do per-variant budgets instead of per-request prewarm because the measurement noise on per-request estimation makes it unstable at scale.
Use slab allocator extension rather than new allocator to minimize rollout risk and reuse existing compaction/eviction paths.
Expose a feature-flag and conservative default off for Dedicated tenants until experiments validate safety across GPU types.
tasks: Extend profiler to record layer-wise KV residency vectors for sample sequences (ENG-927463-A)
Implement estimator that consumes recent shape histograms and model profiles (ENG-927463-B)
Add prewarm slab allocation API and eviction hooks (ENG-927463-C)
Bench harness: replay continuous-batching traces at multiple QPS to validate behavior (ENG-927463-D)
Build dashboards: latency, tokens/sec, GPU free memory, prewarm-enabled ratio, OOM markers (ENG-927463-E)
